title: Certification budget: labelled clusters for a false-accept bound at 1-delta=0.95
protocol: cluster-Hoeffding upper confidence bound on the marginal false-accept rate R(t)=P(accept AND bad): UCB = Rhat + sqrt(ln(1/delta')/(2K)) <= r; K = exchangeable clusters (factories or video clips), delta'=delta for a pre-registered threshold or delta/grid for a union bound over the grid (Z2/LTT). Invert for the largest certifiable r at fixed K.

current_pool.note: all 1,546 unlabelled windows sit in the SAME 47 factories as the 160 labels: the current pool CANNOT add independent clusters. Certification needs NEW factories (new data), not more windows from the existing ones.

certifiable_r_now.interpretation: with 47 factories the tightest certifiable marginal false-accept is ~27% (grid-union) / ~18% (pre-registered threshold) at 95% confidence — a 5% or 10% bound is NOT certifiable today.

implication: Review/error claims: (1) the current 'review 12%, FA 4%' operating point (Z2 coverage 0.85) is DESCRIPTIVE, not certified. (2) To certify FA<=20% at 95% confidence you need ~86 factories (have 47); FA<=10% -> ~342 factories; FA<=5% -> ~1,365 factories (grid-union). A pre-registered single threshold roughly halves-to-quarters those counts (38/150/599). (3) Window-level counts are anti-conservative under within-factory correlation; the cluster (factory) is the honest exchangeable unit. (4) Clip-level labels buy power only if the deployment claim is itself clip-level: there are 58 video clips vs 47 factories, but clips nest inside factories so factory-level remains the safe unit.
